## B — Special Driving Challenges
Audience: English-language first-time standard-license applicants using the Special Driving Challenges section.
Level: beginner study of the selected handbook material, followed by recall and application practice.
Prerequisite policy: understand the cited terminology before comparing exceptions; this is a teaching order, not an extra licensing eligibility requirement.

sections.markdown:
## C — Special Driving Challenges

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A112
Night driving reduces the distance you can see, so search ahead and along both pavement edges. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A112
Use high beams when there is no oncoming traffic, and dim them for an approaching vehicle. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A112
If an approaching driver leaves bright headlights on, look toward the roadway’s right edge instead of staring at the lights. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A112
Use low beams when following another vehicle and in fog, rain or snow. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A112
Keep scanning around the vehicle and beyond the lit area for dark objects or shapes. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A112
Avoid sunglasses and colored lenses at night or on cloudy days because they reduce available light. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A112
At night, the manual advises adding at least 1 second to the following gap. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A112
For unfamiliar roads at night, the manual specifies an addition of at least 2 seconds. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A112
A work zone can include closed lanes, detours and heavy equipment near or on the road. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A113
Slow through a work zone even when workers are absent because narrowed lanes and uneven pavement remain hazards. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A113
Watch work-zone signs, cones, drums, large vehicles and people. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A113
A flashing or sequencing arrow panel can announce a lane closure; slow and move toward the indicated open lane. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A113
Construction warning signs generally show black text or symbols on orange and are often diamond-shaped. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A113
Barricades, vertical panels, concrete barriers, drums and cones guide drivers through construction areas. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A113
Near channeling devices, keep the vehicle centered in its lane and use a responsible speed. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A113
On leaving a work zone, hold your lane and speed and wait until fully clear before changing lanes. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A114
Flaggers use high-visibility clothing, paddles, flags and hand signals to direct traffic; follow their signals patiently. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A114
In a work zone, lower speed, enlarge the following gap and remain ready to stop. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A114
Keep clear of workers and construction vehicles and use extra caution at night even when workers are absent. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A114
Continue following work-zone controls until the End Road Work sign. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A114
Plan for construction delays, leave early and choose another route when possible. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A114
On dirt or gravel, slow and increase the following gap because tire grip is reduced. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A114
On narrow rural roads, slow, stay centered in your lane and watch for oncoming vehicles crowding it. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A114
The single-lane bridge guidance gives the first arriving driver priority and calls for taking turns. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A114
For an open-grating or steel bridge, reduce speed, increase the gap ahead and hold the wheel firmly. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A114
Where woods, crops or hills block the view, slow and prepare to stop. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A114
At a rural intersection without signals or stop/yield signs, approach slowly and be ready for crossing traffic or an oncoming turn. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A115
On slick winter roads, use lower speeds, gentler braking and turns, and a larger following gap. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A115
Before winter weather, check vehicle condition and tires and have antifreeze, hoses, exhaust, battery and brakes inspected. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A115
Use oil suitable for winter conditions and keep battery terminals clean. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A115
At low speed, occasional gentle brake checks can help assess grip and choose an appropriate speed. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A115
Avoid sudden hard braking on slippery pavement because a locked wheel can worsen a skid. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A116
Allow a substantial gap behind the vehicle ahead on snow or ice. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A116
Approach hills and bends more slowly and turn the steering wheel gradually. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A116
Keep windows clear and check that wipers, defroster and headlights work, with enough washer fluid available. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A116
If stuck in snow, avoid spinning the wheels, keep them near straight, clear snow around them and use traction mats, sand or cat litter. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A116
The winter-stranding guidance advises staying with the vehicle while awaiting help. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

Misconceptions: a work zone can remain hazardous when no worker is visible. [A113]
Mnemonic: slow, create space, scan, follow controls.
Glossary: channeling devices guide the path through road works. [A113]
Dynamic facts: equipment, survival, wildlife statistics and cargo-rule currentness require their recorded review.

sections.heading: C2 — Special Driving Challenges
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Special Driving Challenges

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A116
For a winter-stranded vehicle, display a red flag and, if available, warning flares in front and behind. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A116
Use blankets or available warm clothing for yourself and passengers while awaiting winter assistance. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A116
The manual warns to keep snow clear of the exhaust outlet to reduce carbon-monoxide danger. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A116
The suggested winter kit includes a shovel, ice scraper, sand, jumper cables, warm clothes and footwear, plus flares and a red flag. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A116
Drivers of vehicles weighing less than 10,000 pounds must take reasonable measures to keep snow or ice from falling off while driving. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A117
Avoid driving in fog when possible; if travel is necessary, slow enough to stop within the distance you can see. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A117
In fog, use low-beam headlights and road-edge markings for guidance. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A117
If fog makes visibility extremely poor, leave the road, stop with emergency flashers and wait for improvement. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A117
On wet roads, reduce speed, allow more stopping room and avoid sharp turns that can trigger a skid. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A117
The start of light rain can be particularly slick as road oil mixes with water. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A117
Maintain wipers and defroster and use headlights so you can see and be seen in rain. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A117
In rain, signal turns and begin slowing early to give following drivers notice. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A117
Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a water film instead of maintaining road contact. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A117
Reduce hydroplaning risk by slowing in rain, replacing worn tires and maintaining proper inflation. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A118
Do not attempt to drive through a flooded roadway. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A118
Floodwater can conceal an eroded or missing road, with the danger harder to recognize after dark. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A118
If the vehicle stalls in a flooded roadway, the manual directs leaving it promptly and seeking higher ground. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A118
Use extra caution and lower speed at night because darkness restricts visibility. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A118
Wildlife collisions can happen throughout the year, even though the manual describes seasonal peaks. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A118
The pinned manual describes deer-collision increases in autumn with a November peak. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R21 | anchor: A118
The manual identifies May and June as peak moose-collision months and notes autumn incidents too. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R22 | anchor: A118
At night, look for reflected deer eyes and the outline of a moose, whose greater height can hide its eye reflection from headlights. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R23 | anchor: A118
Be especially watchful for moose and deer from dusk to dawn, while remembering an encounter can occur at any hour. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec11-R24 | anchor: A119
Moose and deer signs mark places with concentrated wildlife or a history of collisions. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R25 | anchor: A119
After one deer or moose crosses, watch for others because these animals often move in groups. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R26 | anchor: A119
For a moose near or on the road, slow, remain in the vehicle and allow room and time for it to leave. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R27 | anchor: A119
Do not drive around a moose or get out to watch or chase it away. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R28 | anchor: A119
If impact with an animal is imminent, the initial guidance is to brake and keep steering straight. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R29 | anchor: A119
A passenger-vehicle load must not project beyond the left fenders or more than 6 inches beyond the right fenders. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R30 | anchor: A119
Do not drive with passengers or a load blocking forward or side vision or interfering with control use. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R31 | anchor: A119
Passengers must not sit on the hood, roof or trunk of a moving vehicle. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R32 | anchor: A119
While a vehicle moves on a highway, people may not ride in its trunk or in a camp trailer, mobile home, semitrailer or utility trailer. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R33 | anchor: A119
Pickup passengers younger than 19 must use the passenger compartment, except qualifying work or training travel, licensed-hunter travel to or from hunting, parade participation, or a belted manufacturer-installed outside seat. [A119] [A120]
Source: [A119 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec11-R34 | anchor: A120
On a public way, an open vehicle must secure a dog against falling, jumping or being thrown out, except qualifying farmer or farm-employee agricultural work needing the dog, a hunting dog at a hunting site, or licensed-hunter transport between hunting sites. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> pdf-0120]

sections.heading: D — Special Driving Challenges
sections.markdown:
## D — Special Driving Challenges
Accuracy scope: Special Driving Challenges facts use the pinned official PDF with a registered primary page and any explicitly declared supporting pages; original phrasing preserves actor qualifications, exceptions and modal verbs.
Work-zone sign, panel, channeling and flagger-warning examples on physical113–114 were visually inspected. No unshown signal pose or lane dimension is inferred. [A113] [A114]
The high-beam distance multiplier, winter stopping multiplier, hydroplaning speed bands, flood depths and fatality/collision counts are illustrative or undated and are not exported as universal numeric facts. [A112] [A116] [A117] [A118]
Night following additions are retained in source-specific wording; whether unfamiliar-night additions stack with the ordinary-night addition is not silently decided. [A112]
Universal warm-up timing, non-ABS pumping/clutch instructions, countersteering generalizations, snowbank/bush escape, vehicle rocking and repeated idling need vehicle-specific/current safety review. [A115] [A116]
The blanket no-sleep survival order and claims of idling safety from window opening need current clinical/survival review; exhaust clearance does not guarantee protection from carbon monoxide. [A116]
Wildlife impact brake-release, tail-end aiming and ducking instructions need contemporary safety review before a detailed collision technique is taught. [A119]
The under-nineteen pickup rule explicitly includes its fourth exception across physical119–120; dog-transport exceptions remain complete. Cargo/legal rules are pinned publication statements pending currentness review. [A119] [A120]
Confidence process: every drafted fact received a same-model source-context check before submission; independent coverage and hallucination QA remain pending.
Officeholders, telephone numbers and changing administrative details are excluded from stable learner statements. No source attribution is a legal or clinical signoff.
